clue.text: Napoleon, going to Madrid, oddly ignored cemetery

parts.note: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon Bonaparte

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the city name are dropped, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: The French emperor heads for the Spanish capital and strangely skips a graveyard on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' keeps only the even letters of Madrid. Boney was what the British called Napoleon in the early 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: A boneyard is an informal word for a graveyard, where bones are buried.

clue.text: Work on farm, picking some more apples

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these two words are taken, a run sitting across them

explanation.surface: A farmhand picks a few more apples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points at the run R-E-A-P spanning 'more apples'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut and gather a crop, a classic piece of farm work.

clue.text: Saint resolved to end war

indicators.note: something resolved is worked out or broken down and settled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holy figure has made up his mind to stop the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like determination but signals a rearrangement of ENDWAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew is one of the apostles and the patron saint of Scotland.

clue.text: Cook may use this special shoe

parts.note: a trainer is a sports shoe (a sneaker)

explanation.surface: A chef might wear a particular kind of footwear in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAINER is British English for a sports shoe or sneaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve or colander that a cook uses to drain food.

clue.text: Find you have little time for artist?

parts.note: to trace something is to find or track it down
ye is the old form of you
min is short for minute, a little time

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether discovering you leaves little time for painting.
explanation.walkthrough: TRACEY EMIN is a well-known contemporary British artist, famous for 'My Bed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Emin is a prominent British artist, one of the Young British Artists group.

clue.text: A small bird's behind

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the rear end of a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' is 'is', a link; 'behind' is an adverb here, not a noun for a bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word meaning behind or towards the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Father means to maintain steady speed

definitions.meaning: guv'nor is slang for one's father or the boss
a mechanical regulator on an engine that keeps its speed constant

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a father or boss and also names an engine's speed regulator.

clue.text: In France you may be introduced to foreign currency — that's regularly repeated

indicators.note: being introduced to the currency places the French pronoun inside it

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and Oman
tu is French for you

explanation.surface: A traveller in France might encounter a strange money system that keeps recurring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be introduced to' puts the French pronoun inside the currency; 'that's' is only a link, and the definition is adjectival.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ritual is performed habitually in the same way, a customary repetition.

clue.text: Work on farm, beginning to take old back off

indicators.note: taking the given word away signals it is removed from the longer one
the removal comes off the back, the end of the longer word

parts.note: a threshold is the beginning or outset of something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmhand starts by stripping away an old part from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' is not a first-letter signal: it is THRESHOLD, and the OLD at its end comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To thresh is to beat grain from its husks, a task of farm work.

clue.text: Cannabis taken from empty house by Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the Met is London's police force, abbreviated MP

explanation.surface: Drugs are seized by London police from a vacant property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty house' leaves HE; the Metropolitan Police is London's force.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is the cannabis plant, grown for fibre and as a drug.

clue.text: Professional killer, dodgy character, seen around East End

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed around the final letter
dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so these letters are scrambled
the end of the word East is its last letter

explanation.surface: A hitman, a shady figure, is spotted in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CHARACTER wraps the T from 'East End'. East End is an area of London; 'Professional killer' is a pest catcher, not a hitman.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratcatcher kills rats for a living, so is literally a professional killer.

clue.text: Work on farm with hotel director

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an arrow directs you the way to go

explanation.surface: A farmhand teams up with a hotel manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'director' means a pointer, not a film or company director.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow is to break up and level ploughed soil, farm work.

clue.text: Architectural style queer mason developed

indicators.note: something developed is worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd builder came up with a new way of designing buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' signals rearranging QUEERMASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanesque is a medieval European architectural style with round arches.

clue.text: Troublesome girl and boy not starting to get home by midnight

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: the word loses its starting letter

parts.note: in means at home
the middle of the word night is the letter G

explanation.surface: A girl and boy are a nuisance as they try to be in before twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the middle letter of 'night', G.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoying means irritating or bothersome, much like troublesome.

clue.text: Leslie's crazy about the old girl

indicators.note: about signals turning the whole phrase round

parts.note: Les is short for Leslie; the 's stands for is
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Leslie is wild about his elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Leslie's crazy' as LES MAD; 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an archaic or literary word for a young woman.

clue.text: Reportedly, I refer to the faculty

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by voice, so a spoken form is meant

parts.note: to cite is to refer to, so this is I cite

explanation.surface: Someone says they are referring to the university department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' suggests a university department, but means a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the senses, which are called faculties.

clue.text: Vagrants given transport to outskirts of Paris

parts.note: a tram is a form of transport

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, the outer letters of the city name

explanation.surface: Homeless people are given a ride to the edge of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of Paris' gives PS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are homeless people who wander from place to place, i.e. vagrants.

clue.text: Flower not raised somewhere on Teesside

parts.note: stock is a garden flower

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A bloom fails to grow in a corner of northeast England.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKTON-on-Tees is a town in northeast England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton-on-Tees is a town on the River Tees in the Teesside area.

clue.text: Slow movement of girl taking turn to embrace one

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: embracing puts the single letter inside the other word

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl's dance turn includes a partner's hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' is musical, a section of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is a musical tempo and a slow movement in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Distressed youth? He's kinda cut up

indicators.note: cut up means chopped about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troubled teenager is described as rather upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distressed' puns on de-tressed, with the hair removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead is a youth with a shaven head, so literally without tresses.

clue.text: A bird ascending? It's seen around East Indian state

indicators.note: the reversed letters are placed around the next piece
in a down clue going up means reading backwards

parts.note: a lark is a songbird
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A bird flies up over an Indian region in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: A LARK reversed is KRALA; it goes around E after the K. 'East' is part of the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerala is a state on the southwest coast of India.

clue.text: Work on farm and gain immediate victory

definitions.meaning: to separate grain from chaff by blowing
to triumph at once, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Separating chaff is farm work, and split into two words it means triumph at once.

clue.text: Victor and Michael, director and producer

definitions.meaning: Michael ..., the British film director of Death Wish

explanation.definitionFit: A victor is one who triumphs, and Michael Winner was an English filmmaker.

clue.text: Going ahead with record production and performing

parts.note: a pressing is a batch of records produced from a master
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: Making vinyl and playing live means proceeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing on means continuing or advancing despite difficulty.

clue.text: British sailor comes back from Caucasian capital

indicators.note: coming back signals the whole phrase read backwards

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom, British
AB stands for able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A British sailor returns from a city in the Caucasus.
explanation.walkthrough: UK AB reversed gives the city; 'Caucasian' means in the Caucasus.
explanation.definitionFit: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan, in the Caucasus region.

clue.text: Work on farm, given "Bishop's Tipple"

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ale is a drink, a tipple

explanation.surface: A farmhand is handed a drink called Bishop's Tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To bale is to bundle hay or straw into bales, farm work.

clue.text: Work on farm with seven stars

definitions.meaning: to turn over soil before sowing
the seven bright stars of Ursa Major, the Big Dipper

explanation.definitionFit: Turning soil is farm work, and the Big Dipper asterism has the same British name.

clue.text: Fail to notice remaining gander

parts.note: over means left over or remaining
a gander is a look, a glance

explanation.surface: Someone misses the goose that is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gander' means a look, not a male goose.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to miss it or fail to see it.
